answer: Because the timing is written down against the signal challenge, the walnut audit can replay the haven history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm therefore has to pad 143 submissions and hold every participant open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which forfeits the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. That bill is paid per identity, so 45 aliases cost 340 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
